nodes.question: Is the paper visibly inside the cup, with evidence it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on the rim?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the paper placed inside the cup and visibly stuffed into it. Fail if the paper is only nearby or on the rim, or the image shows no progress toward placing it inside. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is inside and stuffed.
nodes.binding: Assess only the requested paper-in-cup edit, using the image evidence; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
nodes.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Combine the supports under the frozen target: complete only when the paper is visibly inside the cup and evidence shows it has been stuffed into it; absent only when there is no progress toward that requested change; partial when there is some progress but the target is not complete. Unrelated edits are not progress. If required evidence remains insufficient or unresolved, report unknown rather than assuming complete, partial, or absent.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The current node is malformed and underspecified: its binding contains a placeholder and asks only whether the paper is stuffed inside the cup, while the executable criteria require distinguishing complete, partial progress, absent progress, and unresolved evidence. Repair the binding so it faithfully anchors the requested paper-into-cup edit and preserves those distinctions. In this example, the edited image shows a hand holding a paper item near a round object, but the cup and any paper entering it are not clearly identifiable; do not treat the supports’ repeated, high-confidence wording as independent visual confirmation, since s2 depends on s1. Check the source/edited comparison and the actual visible evidence before calling this absent: the source shows a blue cup and white paper, whereas the edited image appears to show a blue printed item and a pink round object, so object identity and whether any requested progress occurred are ambiguous. Route insufficient or conflicting visual evidence to unknown rather than inferring no progress from failure to see the target completed. Keep transport/schema/dependency validity separate from visual judgment; the traces show valid executions, not a transport failure. Preserve the rubric’s partial-progress criterion and avoid adding unsupported visual constraints.
s2: Replace the placeholder binding with a concrete anchor to the requested paper-into-cup edit, and align the node’s question and criteria with the rubric’s three outcomes: complete fulfillment, visible partial progress, and no progress. Do not collapse “not visibly stuffed” into “no change”: inspect the source and edited images for the same objects and any movement toward the requested action. Here, the source shows white paper and a blue cup, while the edit appears to show a blue printed item and a pink round object; their identities and any progress are unclear. That ambiguity warrants unknown, not a confident fail. Keep proximity or rim contact distinct from paper entering the cup, and do not count unrelated edits as progress. The traces are valid executions; their repeated high-confidence judgments are dependent, not independent visual confirmation, so address visual grounding rather than transport or schema validity.
s1: Replace the placeholder binding with a concrete anchor to the requested paper-into-cup edit, and make the node distinguish complete fulfillment, visible partial progress, no progress, and insufficient evidence. Do not equate “not visibly stuffed” with “no change”: compare source and edit for the same paper and cup, and assess whether any visible movement toward placing the paper inside occurred. In these images, the source shows white material beside a blue cup, while the edit shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a pink round object; the objects’ identities and any progress are unclear. That ambiguity should remain unresolved rather than becoming a confident fail. Keep proximity or rim contact distinct from entry into the cup, and do not count unrelated edits as progress. The trace is valid, so address visual grounding and criterion alignment—not transport or schema validity.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence for the requested distinction between paper stuffed inside the cup and paper merely placed inside it. s1 asks for visible evidence of stuffing, but its criteria treat placement inside plus visible stuffing as a pass without defining what evidence establishes stuffing; s2 repeats that same ambiguity rather than checking a distinct, finer condition. The fulfillment readout then relies on those supports to decide completion, partial progress, or absence, so it cannot faithfully distinguish incomplete progress from no progress. The program also makes the fulfillment node active on every s2 status, including unknown, despite its parent being a support check; this is not itself a valid basis for resolving the missing evidence.

The support checks do not establish the requested extent. s3 only tests whether any portion of the paper enters the cup, while s1 and s2 both ask whether it is stuffed inside and do not separately establish a clear completion condition. The fulfillment rule therefore cannot reliably distinguish complete stuffing from partial entry: it treats s3 entry plus failure to establish completion as partial, but s1/s2 may fail or remain unknown without proving incompleteness. This leaves the required complete/partial/absent distinctions under-supported.

The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence for the requested relation. s1 can pass on the broad observation that paper is inside and appears stuffed, but cup_identity only checks whether the source cup can be matched to an edited object; it does not establish that the paper is inside that identified cup. s2 is nested under cup_identity but depends only on s1, so it can assess the relation without the identity evidence that fulfillment says is required. The readout’s identity gate therefore cannot reliably ground the placement evidence, and its fallback to “other saved evidence” does not resolve this gap.

The fulfillment rule is contradictory and can misclassify incomplete progress. It says partial when s1 or entry_extent evidences progress, but entry_extent can pass only when stuffing is established, which s2 also requires for complete; thus a pass on entry_extent cannot coherently mean incomplete progress. Conversely, s1 can fail for no movement while entry_extent is unknown, leaving the readout without a clear composition rule for known negative evidence plus unresolved extent. The support checks also overlap: s2 and entry_extent both assess whether the paper is stuffed into the cup, rather than separating placement from action extent. This does not provide a clean, non-overlapping composition of progress, completion, and uncertainty.

The supports do not establish the requested extent. `entry_extent` passes when any portion of the paper crosses the rim, but the instruction asks for the paper to be stuffed into the cup. The fulfillment rule then treats that entry alone as sufficient for partial, even if the paper is merely partly inserted and there is no evidence of stuffing. Conversely, `s1` and `s2` ask about the same stuffed-inside condition, so requiring both to establish completion does not provide distinct evidence of the missing extent. The program therefore risks crediting insufficient progress and lacks a support check for the extent needed to distinguish stuffing from mere entry.

The fulfillment readout is under-specified and can miscompose the support evidence. `s1` only establishes whether the paper appears inside and stuffed; it does not reliably establish progress when the paper is visibly moving toward the cup but is not yet inside. `identity_progress` can establish that progress, but the fulfillment criteria do not clearly say that its pass alone, together with evidence of incomplete stuffing from `s2`, means partial. They also leave unclear how to distinguish no progress from unresolved evidence when `identity_progress` fails or is unknown. Thus the program does not faithfully define complete/partial/absent/unknown for all relevant evidence combinations.

transaction.reason: The existing supports repeat an ungrounded paper-over-cup interpretation, and their dependent traces are one evidence chain. Repair the coarse support to distinguish identifiable progress from ambiguity, then add a nested check that independently grounds the source paper and cup identities and their edited placement relation. The readout must not treat failure to establish completion as proof of no progress.

actions.question: Compared with the source, does the edited image visibly show the source paper being moved toward or placed into the source cup?
actions.criteria: Pass only if the paper and cup can be identified from the source and the edited image visibly shows an attempted placement or placement relation, including an intermediate attempt. Fail only if the relevant objects and their relationship are clear and show no requested movement or placement. Unknown if object identity or the relationship is ambiguous; do not infer progress or absence from resemblance alone.
actions.binding: Assess only the requested paper-into-cup edit by comparing source and edited images. The source contains a white sheet and blue cup; do not assume an edited object is either one without visible identifying evidence. Exclude unrelated edits.

actions.question: Using the source objects as reference, are the paper and cup identifiable in the edited image, and is their placement relationship clear enough to determine whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed rather than merely near or on its rim?
actions.criteria: Pass if the source paper and cup are identifiable in the edited image and visible evidence establishes the paper inside the cup with evidence of stuffing. Fail if the objects and relation are clear and show the paper not inside or stuffed. Unknown if identity, visibility, or the placement relation is ambiguous; do not infer either completion or absence.
actions.binding: Investigate this specific identity-and-placement proposition using the source and edited images, with s1 as context; independently inspect the images rather than repeating its conclusion. Proximity, contact, or an unverified similar-looking object is not proof of stuffing.

actions.criteria: Use the supports as one evidence chain, not independent corroboration. Complete only if identity_relation passes and the evidence establishes the paper stuffed inside the cup. Partial if s1 passes with identifiable attempted placement or progress but completion is not established; a fail on identity_relation alone does not prove no progress. Absent only when s1 fails on clear evidence of no requested movement or placement. Unknown when necessary identity or progress evidence is unresolved, or when evidence does not support a reliable complete/partial/absent decision. Unrelated edits do not count.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not preserve the requested relation and extent reliably. s1 treats movement toward the cup as a pass, although movement toward it alone is not progress on the requested act of stuffing paper into the cup; the fulfillment rule can then classify that as partial. Also, s2 is redundant and does not add a distinct evidentiary condition, while fulfillment relies on s1 for partial/absent and cup_relation for completion, leaving no sound composition rule for clear evidence of some insertion or stuffing progress that is incomplete. The program therefore risks crediting mere approach as progress and cannot faithfully distinguish partial fulfillment from unresolved evidence.

findings.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup
findings.question: Does the edited image show the requested paper and cup, and is any part of the paper visibly entering or inside the cup?
findings.criteria: Inspect the edited image directly for the paper’s position relative to the cup opening. Distinguish paper merely held above or near the cup from paper entering or inside it; if the cup or its opening is not visible enough to judge, mark unknown.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding a blue-and-white paper object over a rounded pink object; the cup opening is not clearly visible. The source image shows a blue cup and paper, but the edited image’s pink object does not clearly establish that the cup is present.
findings.rationale: The saved checks assert that the paper is held over the cup and not inside, but the edited image does not clearly show a cup or its opening. Directly checking object identity and visibility is needed before treating the reported absence of progress as established; the source image alone cannot establish the edited relation.
